newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stick to plan to repatriate Bosnian refugees.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stick to plan to repatriate Bosnian refugees.

text.p: The Swiss government will press ahead with plans to repatriate thousands of Bosnian refugees even though many cannot return immediately to homes controlled by other ethnic groups, the cabinet said on Monday.
It defended its policy of providing financial assistance to refugees who return voluntarily while holding out the prospect of eventually expelling others who refuse to leave on their own.

The cabinet was replying to a member of parliament who said Berne was undermining the Dayton Accord ending ethnic war in the former Yugoslav republic by sending refugees back without assurances they could again reside in their original home towns.

"If it is not possible to return to the place or origin in which the person's ethnicity is in the minority, Switzerland will support resettlement in a new locale in majority areas...," the government said in its response.
"Temporary accomodation in majority areas is also made possible until the definitive return to their area of origin."
The move was a setback for Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, who had criticised Switzerland's approach in an internal document published by the SonntagsZeitung weekly at the weekend.

"Forcibly repatriating people to an area that is not where they come from in a region where they make up the ethnic majority means actively supporting ethnic cleansing and contradicting Dayton, the UNHCR (refugee agency) and the community of nations," he wrote.

But Justice Minister Arnold Koller fought the idea of giving special treatment to refugees whose home towns were controlled by ethnic adversaries, saying this would require complicated and costly procedures, the newspaper said.
The cabinet decided in January to start sending back single people and childless couples among the 18,000 Bosnian refugees in Switzerland, most of them Moslems.
Nearly 3,000 of the 6,300 people affected had returned voluntarily by May 23, officials said. The deadline for them to leave expired on April 30.
Many others have sought permission to extend their stay, but Berne has threatened to use force to expel people still here without permission by the end of August.
Around 15,000 Bosnian refugees still live in Switzerland.
